title: Design System: Where Them Logs App

display.purpose: The home headline drawn as a path with accent slashes, and reading-page titles.

headline.purpose: Page titles on results, app and vendor pages, and nothing-found headings.

title.purpose: The app name on a result card.

body.purpose: Prose. Wraps with the window; never capped in ch.

label.purpose: Section names, counts, qualifiers and footer links in sentence case with tabular figures.

path.purpose: Log paths in mono, wrapping anywhere, selected whole on one click.

code-tag.purpose: Installer and architecture tags, keyboard keys, path previews.

shadows.name: shadow
shadows.purpose: Light theme. Only for layers that float over the page: suggestions, share menu, consent bar.

shadows.name: shadow-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark theme value of the same token.

motion.name: ease-rack
motion.purpose: The system's one easing. The token name is a legacy name.

motion.name: rack-in
motion.purpose: The one keyframe: opacity 0.35 to 1 with a 6px rise. Result cards on load, and the copy confirmation.

motion.name: disclosure-turn
motion.purpose: The arrow on a file list turning when it opens.

motion.name: confirm-hold

narrative.overview:
A log path is a folder location, so the site is a folder you look things up in. The ground is calm: pale cool grey in light, deep navy in dark. On it sits one manila tab colour, used for every fill the visitor acts on: the search field, the current filter, the main button, the file at the end of a path. Everything else is white or navy cards with hairline borders, grey text, and paths set in mono.

The page is simple on purpose. The visitor already knows the app name and is usually in the middle of fixing something. One search field does the work, the answer appears under it with a copy button beside each path, and nothing competes with that. There are no gradients, no uppercase labels, no condensed type, and one soft shadow that only appears under things that float over the page.

Light and dark are both first-class. Each follows the visitor's device and there is no switch. Every colour is a token with a value for each theme, so a new screen that uses only tokens is correct in both without extra work.

The admin pages run on the same tokens and the same parts (cards, the manila field, toggles, buttons), laid out denser: a list rail beside the record, rows split by hairlines.
keyCharacteristics: One manila tab colour for every fill you act on, always with dark brown text on it
Calm ground, surface cards with hairline borders, gaps between cards
Bricolage Grotesque for words, Spline Sans Mono for paths, type tags and keys
Soft corners at 10px and 6px; flat fills with no gradients
Light and dark from the device, every colour a token with both values
One motion: cards rise and fade in once

rules.name: The Token Pair Rule
rules.body: Every colour is a token with a light value and a dark value. No hex, rgb or named colour is written in a component. If a new colour is needed, add the token with both values first.

rules.name: The Tab Fill Rule
rules.body: `tab` is for fills only and always carries `tabfg` text (with `tabdim` for the quiet text on the same fill). It is never a text colour on the ground, because manila on pale grey cannot be read. The one inverse is the Search button inside the field: a `tabfg` fill with `tab` text, so the pair is the same.

rules.name: The Accent Text Rule
rules.body: Coloured text uses `accent`. In dark, `accent` and `tab` happen to share a value; in light they do not. Keep them as two tokens and never swap one for the other.

rules.name: The Device Theme Rule
rules.body: Themes follow the device's colour scheme. There is no theme switch, no stored preference and no theme class to set.

rules.name: The Marker Rule
rules.body: Platform colours are small blocks only and never carry text. A platform is always also named in words or by its code, and its marker has its own pattern, so colour is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque for words. Spline Sans Mono for what the machine wrote or reads: paths, file names, type tags, keys, inline code. Labels and counts are words, so they stay in Bricolage with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase transforms and no letter-spaced labels. Labels are plain words in sentence case; only headings carry tracking, and it is negative.

rules.name: The Open Measure Rule
rules.body: Text blocks are never width-capped in `ch`. Prose wraps with the window or its column; a column is sized by the layout (in rem or grid tracks), not by a character count on the text. The file list under a path sizes its columns to the longest file name; that is a layout track, not a text cap.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is one shadow token and it marks one thing: this layer floats over the page. Cards, buttons and hover states never take a shadow.

rules.name: The Whole Path Rule
rules.body: The tree is presentation only. A path is never expanded, edited or shortened; environment variables stay as written, and every copy button copies the full stored path, however it is drawn.

rules.name: The One Motion Rule
rules.body: One keyframe: a rise of 6px with a fade from 0.35 to full, 320ms on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`. Result cards use it once on load, staggered 30ms per card up to the eighth; the copy confirmation reuses it. The only other movement is a disclosure arrow turning (160ms). Reduced-motion preference turns all of it off.

dos: Do write interface copy in plain words: search, add, delete, platform, log locations. Class names such as plate, zone, rack, scan and sheet are legacy names in the code only; they never appear in what a visitor reads and they say nothing about how a thing should look.
Do give every colour as a token with a light and a dark value, and check a new screen in both themes.
Do use the manila `tab` for fills you act on or that mark the current choice, with `tabfg` text on it.
Do use `accent` for coloured text, links, focus rings and thin signals.
Do set paths, file names, type tags and keys in Spline Sans Mono, and everything else in Bricolage Grotesque.
Do print paths exactly as stored and let them wrap; give each one its own copy button.
Do let text wrap with the window or its layout column.
Do separate cards with space and split rows inside a container with a `line` hairline.
Do keep the consent buttons identical.
donts: Don't use `tab` as a text colour on the ground, or put any text other than `tabfg` or `tabdim` on a tab fill.
Don't add a theme switch or store a theme choice. The device decides.
Don't write a raw colour value in a component.
Don't cap a text block's width in `ch`.
Don't use uppercase or letter-spaced labels, condensed type, or a third typeface.
Don't add gradients, or a shadow on anything that does not float over the page.
Don't colour text with a platform colour, or show a platform by colour alone.
Don't announce a copy with a toast; say it beside the button.
Don't reuse the folder tab as a small label above other content. It belongs to the search field.
Don't add hover lifts, scale effects or scroll reveals. One motion is the whole grammar.
Don't bring back warehouse words or looks: no stencil caps, hazard stripes, square steel plates or signal cyan.
